standard_prerequisites.name: The standing situation (axioms A, B, C)
standard_prerequisites.statement: A dg category with the distinguished-triangle axioms, in particular the admissible short exact sequence attached to a morphism by axiom (C) and the associated triangle (the author's Situation situation-ABC, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: Axiom (C) supplies the sequence x -> C(alpha) -> x[1] and the structure maps b, p, s, pi, sigma used throughout (source lines 4327-4349, 4382-4410).

standard_prerequisites.name: Cone of a morphism and its triangle
standard_prerequisites.statement: The cone C(f) of a morphism with its inclusion, projection and the triangle it forms, and the notion of a morphism of triangles.
standard_prerequisites.use: The cone is the object being compared and the conclusion is an isomorphism of triangles (source lines 4331-4349, 4362-4377).

standard_prerequisites.name: Null homotopy of the identity of a cone
standard_prerequisites.statement: The identity morphism on the cone of an identity is homotopic to zero (the author's lemma lemma-id-cone-null, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is invoked at the end of part (1) to conclude the homotopy equivalence (source lines 4463-4466).

standard_prerequisites.name: Factorisation of a morphism through an admissible monomorphism
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every morphism factors through an admissible monomorphism which extends to an admissible short exact sequence (the author's lemma lemma-factor).
standard_prerequisites.use: Part (2) applies it to alpha and transfers the isomorphism of triangles (source lines 4350-4377).

core_obligations: Set up the larger diagram for part (1) without the sign change on the connecting map, and recall the identities among the structure maps that the standing situation provides (source lines 4382-4410).

Define the candidate maps e = beta p and f = b s - sigma delta and verify by explicit matrix computations that they are inverse up to homotopy, using the identities among the structure maps and their differentials (source lines 4409-4462).

Check the compatibility with the triangle structure and conclude: verify that the right square of the diagram commutes up to homotopy (referring to the retained null-homotopy lemma for the identity of a cone) so that the displayed morphism is an isomorphism of triangles (source lines 4463-4489).

Transfer to part (2): apply the author's factorisation lemma to an arbitrary morphism alpha, identify the factored sequence with an admissible short exact sequence, and carry the isomorphism of triangles across it (source lines 4350-4377 with the corresponding part of the proof).

proof_roadmap.step: Write the larger diagram and collect the structure-map identities.
Define e and f and prove they are mutually inverse up to homotopy by matrix computations.
Check the right square, invoke the null-homotopy lemma, and conclude the isomorphism of triangles.
For part (2), factor an arbitrary morphism and transfer the result.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-cone-homotopy at source lines 4325-4379: in the standing situation, (1) an admissible short exact sequence x -> y -> z determines a homotopy equivalence e : C(alpha) -> z making the displayed diagram an isomorphism of triangles in the homotopy category, where x -> C(alpha) -> x[1] is the admissible sequence supplied by axiom (C); and (2) for an arbitrary morphism alpha : x -> y, using the factorisation of alpha through an admissible monomorphism given by the author's factorisation lemma, there is an isomorphism of triangles between the triangle of the factored sequence and the triangle of the cone of alpha. The proof at source lines 4381-4489 is a long explicit computation and is genuinely research-level in its bookkeeping. For part (1) it writes down a larger diagram without the sign change on the connecting map, defines the two maps e = beta p and f = b s - sigma delta explicitly, verifies by matrix computations that they are inverse up to homotopy (which consumes several identities among the structure maps, the differentials and the connecting morphisms), and then checks that the right square of the diagram commutes and that the resulting morphism of triangles is an isomorphism, referring to the earlier null-homotopy computation for the identity of a cone. Part (2) transfers the result across the factorisation. Every equality is a separate computation and the statement gives none of them. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
